races.name: Burke's Clonbur 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Divine Believer
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's hold-up runner is the Strand top selection at low confidence; five flat runs on Good ground without a win or place on similar going is a genuine concern, and the step up to 2m2f hurdles from a flat background needs proving at this level.

runners_data.name: Another Day Done
runners_data.note: Strand danger; has placed four times at 10f on Good and recorded a win on Standard, so this hurdling debut over 2m2f stretches the stamina profile, though McCann's record of 1/4 in 14 days shows a trainer striking while the iron is hot.

runners_data.name: Chairmanforlife
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's prominent runner has four hurdle starts showing a best of 4th at 13f on Good; likely to travel close to the pace and her positional profile suits a Montevetro-led scenario, though 0 wins from 4 sim-going runs requires respect.

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 82 and the only runner with an actual hurdles win (1/10f/SOF); wears a tongue-tie, and Cromwell's 0/38 in 14 days is flat but the horse's class and prominent style make her the most naturally placed to exploit a steady gallop.

runners_data.name: Point Star
runners_data.note: A single hurdle run (4th, 18f, Good) for Mark Fahey is thin evidence, but the midfield profile and 14 days since last run suggest a trainer who believes he's ready; the 7lb claimer Thomas O'Connor adds some uncertainty over 2m2f in a busy field.

runners_data.name: Armillary
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Miss Tara Lee Cogan with no going data; lightly raced flag warrants treating this as a complete unknown — impossible to assess pace or stamina profile without a recorded run.

runners_data.name: Camp Verde
runners_data.note: Hanlon's runner has form of 0U8 in three hurdle starts, all on Good; a true hold-up type reshuffled into a midfield berth he's unlikely to hold naturally, and with no wins or places from three sim-going runs his chance must be discounted while he finds his feet in this discipline.

runners_data.name: Step By Step
runners_data.note: Another debut runner for Aidan Anthony Howard wearing hood; the trainer strikes at 1/2 in 14 days which is a positive signal, but there is simply no performance data available on going or trip to project a race shape.

runners_data.name: Wills History
runners_data.note: Unraced on public record for Brian McMahon; the 0/5 trainer 14-day strike rate and absence of any form string make this a speculative runner in a competitive 16-horse maiden.

runners_data.name: We're Out Of Aces
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's unraced runner carries the yard's 4/33 14-day form — the best stable strike rate on show — which is the only meaningful pointer; no going, trip, or style data to work with beyond that powerful training angle.

runners_data.name: Bell Ex Too
runners_data.note: Cody's hold-up type hasn't run in 42 days and has five runs all between 10-14f on various surfaces without a win or place; stepping up to 2m2f hurdles is a significant ask, and the long freshener is a flag rather than a positive.

runners_data.name: Montevetro
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and therefore crucial to how this entire shape unfolds; has led and placed at 10f on Standard twice but 2m2f is a sharp stamina test, and Denis Hogan's 0/25 in 14 days means the win expectation rests more on dictating than on outright class.

runners_data.name: Neon Eyes
runners_data.note: Cromwell's second runner; fresh off a 6-day turnaround wearing a hood, with a best of 2nd at 10f on Good — the hold-up profile gets crowded in this field and the quick return after that run needs to be respected as a stamina question.

runners_data.name: Sonny Corleone
runners_data.note: Elliott's hold-up type has four flat runs between 7-14f on Good or Standard with a best of 4th; 37 days since last run is workmanlike, but without hurdles experience confirmed and no sim-going wins, he is firmly in the speculative column.

runners_data.name: Matada
runners_data.note: Cromwell's third runner and longest absentee at 111 days; form reads 14th, 12th, 11th in three hurdle starts — a hold-up type mapped to midfield through redistribution and whose prior record on similar going provides no positive angle.

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Meade's runner is another genuine hold-up horse forced into a midfield berth; wears a breast-girth and has finished between 6th-11th in six hurdle starts on Good, so while the yard fires at 1/32 recently, the style displacement and weak form history significantly reduce the scenario in which he features.

races.paceDynamic: Montevetro is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-horse maiden and, with no other natural leader to challenge him for the lead, he should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe. The pace is unlikely to be scorching — one uncontested leader over 2m2f in this company typically sets a measured tempo that rewards horses travelling well in behind rather than pure closers grinding from the back. Captain Con, Matada, and Camp Verde are genuine hold-up types that the map has redistributed to midfield, meaning the field carries a heavy cluster of horses that will sit in a similar position, creating traffic and potential trouble in running for all three. The race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent or off-the-pace hunters who can track Montevetro at close range and pounce in the straight — horses like Misty Cove and Chairmanforlife, who can hold a prominent pitch, are better placed than the true hold-up brigade squeezed into midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Montevetro Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Montevetro leads unchallenged and sets a fair but undemanding gallop, allowing a prominent tracker to stride past in the straight.
scenarios.body: Montevetro's steady tempo gives horses travelling just behind him a significant energy advantage entering the final climb, with no pace battle to burn them out early; Misty Cove and Chairmanforlife, both with the positional profile to sit second or third, are ideally placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Two Stay
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate gallop becomes a dawdle and the race turns into a sprint from the final hurdle, suiting whoever is handiest at the top of the straight.
scenarios.body: A false pace over 2m2f with 16 runners compresses the field and the winner is most likely the horse sitting closest to Montevetro with enough class to outstay him on the run-in; Misty Cove's higher OR of 82 and prior win form give her the edge in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a clear late run for a closer coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Divine Believer, the Strand top selection, is the most credible beneficiary given De Bromhead's training hand and a staying profile, though her flat-form history and zero wins/places on similar going temper expectations; Another Day Done has placed at this trip on comparable ground and could emerge if gaps open.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Cause Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the midfield becomes congested with redistributed hold-up horses and the race breaks up into scrimmaging groups, producing a chaotic finish.
scenarios.body: Camp Verde, Matada, and Captain Con all seeking similar ground in a compressed midfield raises the risk of interference and allows an unchallenged Montevetro or a wide-travelling prominent horse to benefit; this scenario has the lowest probability precisely because those three are racing out of their natural role and are unlikely to deliver in a shape that requires positioning they won't naturally achieve.

watchPoints.text: Montevetro sets the entire race tempo alone — if he quickens or kicks unexpectedly on the back straight, horses like Misty Cove and Chairmanforlife must be close enough to respond or the race is effectively over.

Camp Verde, Captain Con, and Matada are all genuine hold-up types compressed into midfield — watch for early scrimmaging and interference as 16 runners jostle for position in the first mile; any horse drawn wide could be checked or carried wide at the first bend.

Another Day Done and Divine Believer are both hold-up types making hurdling debuts or stepping up sharply in trip — if the pace is as steady as expected, they may find themselves with too much ground to make up off Montevetro's honest-but-modest gallop.

We're Out Of Aces represents the Gordon Elliott yard, which carries the strongest 14-day strike rate of any trainer in this field (4/33); debutants from top yards at odds deserve monitoring in the market in the hour before post.
Neon Eyes has turned around in just six days — watch the market to see if Cromwell runs her fresh with a specific purpose or if this is a fitness spin before a bigger target.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Brave Lady
runners_data.note: OR 110, the class standout; consistently placed in this grade and trip on Good and Soft, making her supremely reliable in these conditions, and her prominent style should see her land a forward position once the initial scrimmage settles — Strand Scorecard lists her as chief danger.

runners_data.name: The Dotski
runners_data.note: De Bromhead-trained prominent runner returning from 195 days off; the layoff is a significant unknown, though two reasonable placed efforts on Healy track give a reasonable baseline — fitness the key question on debut back.

runners_data.name: Goodgollymissholly
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Good going and placed over 18f; the tongue-tie is noted, and Elliott's yard is in decent form — her prominent style suits the expected race shape and she has proven she handles this ground well.

runners_data.name: Rosarian
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who placed over 19f on Good to give confidence over this trip; prominent style should see her well-positioned, though she's a maiden in a competitive field and the Halley yard has a modest 14-day record.

runners_data.name: Lunar Majesty
runners_data.note: Murphy-trained mare who has placed just once in seven runs on similar going; her prominent tag flatters a horse who has struggled to build on that third at Sligo, and the record suggests limited progress available.

runners_data.name: Maximillian Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has been off 88 days; placed over 16f on Soft and has shown ability, but the lengthy absence and a hold-up style in a race likely to have traffic issues creates risk — needs a clear passage.

runners_data.name: Katie Can't Count
runners_data.note: Mullins inmate with a front-running instinct who is remapped to midfield by pace congestion in this 18-runner field; her form is limited to two runs, and racing against her natural grain diminishes her chance in this shape.

runners_data.name: Ronnie's Rascal
runners_data.note: Young Mullins four-year-old with two placed efforts on Good going at 22f and 18f; prominent style and some stamina evidence make her interesting, though the 7lb claimer and a competitive market suggest she's a horse to follow rather than back blindly here.

runners_data.name: Hashtag Doyen
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old midfield type whose sole comparable run produced a 4th on Good at 16f — limited upside at this rating but an uncomplicated profile and could pick up minor money if chaos develops at the back.

runners_data.name: Lexenna
runners_data.note: OR 57 and winless; genuinely enjoys racing prominently but is pushed back by the field's surplus of pace-seeking types, meaning she's unlikely to find the natural rhythm that suits her — low expectations are warranted.

runners_data.name: Tara Boe
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a hood who loves to race up with the pace but faces the same positional squeeze as other prominent types here; her lone run on comparable going produced a remote 8th, and nothing in the profile encourages optimism.

runners_data.name: Santa Paula
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with two third-place finishes on Good going, both over shorter; prominent style and proven placed form give her each-way claims if she gets a clean trip, though 22f looked beyond her last time.

runners_data.name: Certosa
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has placed at 16f on Good; 20 days since last run is fine, and a 7lb claimer rides — her hold-up style is well-suited to the expected race shape if she can jump cleanly and get the gaps she needs late.

runners_data.name: Mia In Milan
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has not troubled the judge in three runs on Good going at distances up to 22f; 94 days off and modest form make her a long-shot, though the style suits a late-run race shape.

runners_data.name: Kilbarry Alexy
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, returning from 251 days off; will set the pace on a comfortable lead, but is rated just 62 and her stamina over 2m2f after such a break is untested — the leader by default, not by merit.

runners_data.name: Sea Limit
runners_data.note: Midfield type rated 57 with two ninth-place finishes on Good; no obvious angle to recommend her in a competitive mares' maiden, and 20 days since last run is not a concern but ability appears the limiting factor.

runners_data.name: Mastertown Miss
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard's top selection at medium confidence; hold-up four-year-old who placed over 16f on Soft and on Good going, giving strong ground evidence, and trainer Kelly is in form over 14 days — well-placed to pounce if the race sets up as expected.

runners_data.name: Carleys Lilly
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up mare with four placed finishes in five runs on Good going, all at 16f-18f, suggesting this 2m2f trip could be a slight stretch — if she stays, her reliable profile and course-going evidence make her a solid each-way proposition.

races.paceDynamic: Kilbarry Alexy is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to press hard from the off, she will control the tempo from the front on what looks a comfortable, measured gallop over 2m2f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe. The surplus of prominent-minded types — Brave Lady, Goodgollymissholly, Ronnie's Rascal, Santa Paula and Rosarian — will jostle for the immediate positions behind her, creating a competitive early order but without meaningfully lifting the pace into a true test. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural berth; Katie Can't Count, Tara Boe and Lexenna are genuine pace-seeking horses who are most likely to find themselves shuffled back against their instincts, reducing their effectiveness. The resulting shape — a controlled lead, a crowded mid-pack, and a clean run available to hold-up types off a sustainable tempo — strongly favours hold-up horses with a proven turn of foot on this ground, as the race is likely to set up for a late surge rather than reward those who committed early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Kilbarry Alexy dictates an uncontested, moderate pace and hold-up horses get a clean passage to produce their finish.
scenarios.body: Kilbarry Alexy bowls along in front unchallenged while the hold-up brigade track the large field through the final circuit; as the pace lifts at the second-last, horses produced widest or with the clearest route sweep past the tiring prominent types.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early jostling among prominent runners is resolved quickly and a compact lead group sets an honest enough gallop that suits those racing handily.
scenarios.body: With Brave Lady and Goodgollymissholly securing the best positions behind Kilbarry Alexy, the race is run at a pace that tests stamina and rewards those who travel fluently in the first half-dozen; a hold-up horse who gets into trouble in traffic is left with too much to do.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Kilbarry Alexy's modest gallop is never meaningfully challenged and the field concertinas, allowing one prominent runner to steal clear unchallenged at the last.
scenarios.body: A slow, tactical affair sees Kilbarry Alexy slowing the race to a crawl before brave jumping at the last launches one of the handy types into an unassailable lead; hold-up horses find the finish-line arrives too soon for their run to land.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Suits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded prominent group causes interference or fallers, opening a route for a previously unfancied runner to come through on the wide outside.
scenarios.body: With up to 18 runners scrambling for position on an undulating track, a big-field mares' maiden can produce a surprise if key fancies are squeezed or badly hampered at a crucial hurdle; a horse with clean jumping and a patient jockey benefits most.

watchPoints.text: Brave Lady is the highest-rated runner (OR 110) with a flawless record of placed finishes on this ground and trip — if she secures a prominent position early and jumps cleanly, she has the class to win and her market move should be monitored closely.

The 18-runner field with a glut of prominent types — Brave Lady, Goodgollymissholly, Ronnie's Rascal, Santa Paula — will create significant early crowding; watch for interference or horses losing position at the first two hurdles, which could compromise several fancied runners.

Kilbarry Alexy returns from 251 days off as the sole front-runner — if she tires significantly before the last, a sudden pace collapse could catch prominent horses flat-footed and hand the race to the closers far earlier than expected.

Mastertown Miss (Strand top pick) and Carleys Lilly are both hold-up types whose chance depends entirely on getting a clean run through the field in the straight — watch at the top of the home turn for whether they have daylight or are hemmed in.

Katie Can't Count, Tara Boe and Lexenna are all naturally front-running horses remapped to midfield by the race's pace congestion — if any of them secure a forward berth early despite the crowd, their odds may significantly understate their chance in that specific shape.

races.paceDynamic: Affinity Rock is the confirmed front-runner and, with no confirmed rival to press her, she is likely to control tempo from the outset at a pace that suits her stamina on Good to Yielding ground over 2m7f. The prominent congestion is real — Carried With Love, Straight Home, Joya Del Mar, and Survivors Sister all want to race prominently, meaning the first two furlongs will see jostling for position that could briefly elevate the early pace before Affinity Rock settles into her rhythm. Giorgia Rose and Cherry Red are genuine prominent types by nature but are mapped to midfield because the prominent berths are already over-subscribed; they are unlikely to secure their preferred position and their chances are tempered accordingly. This race shape — a controlled front-runner, a compressed prominent group, and a moderately stamina-testing trip in soft-ish ground — favours horses who can track the pace in the first three or four positions without burning energy in traffic, then sustain a finish from the second-last fence; it is a race for prominent trackers with proven stamina rather than hold-up horses or pure speedsters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Affinity Rock Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock dictates a sustainable pace unchallenged and the prominent group fails to sustain a meaningful challenge from 2 out.
scenarios.body: Affinity Rock bowls along in front at a tempo that suits her 0W3P placed record at this trip and going, with the prominent pack burning energy tracking her; she has the race set up perfectly for a front-running performance that her Good-to-Soft record fully supports.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock's pace is just high enough to stretch the field but leaves her vulnerable on the run-in, allowing a close-tracking prominent horse to collar her.
scenarios.body: A runner sitting second or third, conserving energy behind Affinity Rock, produces a sustained run from the second-last to wear her down on the long Ballinrobe straight; the Good to Yielding surface rewards those who settle and finish rather than those who fight for early position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Produces Shock
scenarios.trigger: If the four-way battle for prominent positions burns the pace early and leaves a calmer, well-settled tracker to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Early scrapping between Straight Home, Joya Del Mar, Survivors Sister and Carried With Love for the two or three best positions behind Affinity Rock unsettles several of them; a horse that has found a clean run and raced within herself emerges fresh at the business end.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Capitalise on Strong Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If early scrimmaging drives the overall pace high enough to compromise the front-runners and prominent group, opening the door for hold-up types.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires either Cooke's Lass or Ad Caelum to produce an unusually powerful late run, something neither has shown consistently, and both are racing from styles that are genuinely off the pace rather than redistributed prominent types; the probability is low because the confirmed pace is described as sustainable, not suicidal.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a scrappy opening half-mile as Carried With Love, Straight Home, Joya Del Mar, and Survivors Sister all attempt to slot in behind Affinity Rock — traffic incidents and interference are plausible between the 1st and 3rd fences.

Cooke's Lass returns after a full calendar year off; if she shows signs of distress or lack of fitness early, Kevin Sexton may be forced to pull up, which could unsettle runners immediately behind her at a fence.

Giorgia Rose and Cherry Red, both natural prominent types pushed into midfield by the overcrowded pace positions, may attempt to force their way forward in the early stages — creating a pocket of congestion in the 4th-to-6th place area on the first circuit.

Joya Del Mar's track record at Ballinrobe is the strongest course-specific angle in the race; watch where Alix Balfe positions her after the first bend — if she secures a clean prominent slot, her finishing record at this venue becomes a live factor from 2 out.

Affinity Rock's early position and Millar's early pace judgement are central to how the race shapes — if she bowls along clearly, the race is hers to lose; if she is crowded or harried in the first few furlongs, the dynamics shift materially in favour of the prominent trackers.

races.paceDynamic: Kilashee is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field over 2m7f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe, and with the flag-bearers fades-in-finish tag, the pace is unlikely to be punishing — expect a controlled, measured gallop that keeps the field together through the early stages before the tempo builds from the third-last fence. Fr Gilligansvoyge, Las Brisas Boy, Hit The Frame and Reve Inoui are genuine prominent types and will press forward to track Kilashee closely, creating a small competitive lead group without triggering a true breakaway pace. The field contains significantly more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Three Tribes, Swing Time, Set The Tone, The Little Yank and U Asking Me are all natural closers, but with so many competitors needing to settle back, the most likely to genuinely secure their preferred off-the-pace position are Ladies Well and Il Silenzio given their class and stable management, while the redistributed runners will be crowded into mid-division rather than sitting last. A steady-to-fair gallop over this stamina trip on easy ground strongly favours hold-up horses with proven stamina who can travel smoothly in mid-to-rear and produce a sustained challenge from the second-last — tactical riders who can save their horse's energy early will have the clearest path.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If Kilashee sets a sustainable gallop and the true hold-up horses find clear runs from the second-last fence.
scenarios.body: The measured tempo across 2m7f on yielding ground plays into the hands of horses with stamina and class who have been able to travel comfortably through the race; the final climb home on this circuit will expose those ridden cold and reward those with a smooth pick-up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Las Brisas Boy and Fr Gilligansvoyge push forward aggressively to press Kilashee and the pace becomes strung out.
scenarios.body: A contested lead raises the gallop sufficiently to stretch the field, benefiting horses who travel prominently and jump fluently under pressure; Fr Gilligansvoyge's consistent form figures and course-appropriate profile make it particularly dangerous in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinders Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems bog down the top hold-up performers and the race is won from a mid-pack, grinding position off the final turn.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners, congestion in the straight is a real risk, and horses who travel mid-division with tactical riders can slip through gaps that deeper-seated closers cannot reach; Not So Serious, fresh from a recent win, and Island McCoo with course experience are well-placed in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Kilashee dictates completely unchallenged and the prominent horses fail to close the gap home.
scenarios.body: Despite the fades-in-finish tag, if the field is so large and traffic-ridden that no horse can mount a clean challenge, a horse in front jumping well may simply last home; this is the least likely shape given Kilashee's profile and the quality of closers behind.

watchPoints.text: Ladies Well is the Scorecard top selection and carries the strongest sim-going profile in the race (2W4P from 8 runs on comparable ground) — watch how Alan O'Sullivan settles her in the first half mile, as a clean passage from mid-rear into the straight is the key requirement.

Fr Gilligansvoyge has posted form figures of 132112 and is the most consistent prominent-type jumper in the field — if the 13-year-old is travelling smoothly jumping the final ditch, it has the jumping fluency and stamina to steal a march on the closers.

With 19 runners in a 2m7f handicap chase, traffic congestion approaching the final two fences is almost certain — horses drawn wide or blocked in mid-division (Three Tribes, Set The Tone, Mistyburn) may suffer interference that nullifies their finishing kick regardless of how well they are travelling.

Kilashee's fades-in-finish flag at 2m7f on yielding ground is the key pace regulator — if Kevin Healy (7) allows the field to coast for the first circuit, the lack of pressure may compress the field and deny the better closers the conditions they need to pick them off.

Il Silenzio at OR 100 is the highest-rated runner in the field and has a jockey booking for a yard at T14:0/2 — worth watching in the market; if supported, it signals trainer Martin Brassil believes the 38-day break has the horse primed for this sharp-end assignment.

runners_data.name: Custers Mistake
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 9-year-old (401 days off) with unknown going suitability and an unclassified style — Peter McCreery has zero runners in 14 days and the long layoff raises serious fitness doubts despite a recent win in the form string.

runners_data.name: Leave In Secret
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Thomas Gibney, 0 wins from 3 similar-going placed efforts, who will force the pace from the off; carrying top weight (166lbs) after running 34 days ago and the strong early gallop he helps create may undermine his own stamina.

runners_data.name: Farrokh
runners_data.note: Barry Connell's 7-year-old ran 14 days ago and won over 16f on Good going, showing sharp recent form (46U-14); a prominent racer who must avoid getting caught in the eight-runner scrum early or that finishing kick will be spent by the home straight.

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: The Scorecard's top selection, a hold-up horse with excellent sim-going form (10/10 starts, 1W3P) trained by John Patrick Ryan who has been in cracking form (2/14 over 14 days); at OR 93 he has a favourable weight (149lbs) and Kevin Healy's claiming allowance adds value — the strong pace suits his patient style ideally, though low confidence is noted given competitive field.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Arizona
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with four places from nine sim-going runs but zero wins; the 23-day turnaround is fine but OR 93 and a field full of similar types means he must find improvement to justify punter faith.

runners_data.name: Claude
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner wearing a tongue tie and bit, trained by Sarah Joanna Connell, who shapes to battle directly with Mo Ghille Mar and Leave In Secret from the first fence; his form shows three out-of-frame efforts recently and the brutal early duel will likely see him swallowed up before the second circuit is done.

runners_data.name: Stoneyford Lady
runners_data.note: Key danger per the Scorecard — De Bromhead's 7-year-old mare wears a tongue tie and has an excellent sim-going record (7/8, 1W4P); Danny Power's 4lb claim is a useful aid and 45 days since her last run suggests she arrives fresh, capable of tracking the pace without being embroiled in the early scrum.

runners_data.name: Roccabaker
runners_data.note: 145 days off the track is a significant concern for this midfield-styled 8-year-old; David Harry Kelly had 2 winners from 12 in 14 days so the yard is alive, and he won at 22f on Soft suggesting stamina is no issue if fitness holds.

runners_data.name: Sayitfirst
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with genuine stamina credentials (won at 16f, placed at 16f twice on sim going, 7/7 record); Darren Collins has him fit after 32 days and the patient style of Michael Kenneally suits a race where the pace will be honest — could be overlooked at a big price.

runners_data.name: Political Stance
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with very limited sim-going evidence (2/3 runs) and no wins or places to his name on comparable ground; the trainer has only 1 winner from 5 in 14 days and without a jockey name listed, this is a significant flag.

runners_data.name: Bossing It
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from David O'Brien's yard (0/1 in 14 days) who has placed twice from eight sim-going runs; the 26-day gap is manageable and the honest headgear-free profile means Josh Williamson can ride him cold — benefits from the hot pace but needs a clear run late.

runners_data.name: Ballybrittas
runners_data.note: Midfield-positioned P.J. Rothwell runner who won last time over 16f on Good going and has strong sim-going form (5/5, 1W2P); R. Sugrue's 4lb claim helps at 160lbs and the 34-day gap is fine — a horse with quiet claims who could emerge from a strong-run race.

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who won last time out over 18f on Good going, trained by John Joseph Hanlon and wearing a hood; confirmed front-runner with the best sim-going record of the pace-setters (11/12, 2W2P) — if he can steal first run from Leave In Secret and Claude he is the primary threat to hold on.

runners_data.name: Lady Doyanne
runners_data.note: Scorecard danger from De Bromhead's powerful yard (4/26 in 14 days); a consistent prominent racer with three consecutive runner-up finishes, going OK across seven runs (0W3P) and wearing a tongue tie — Alan O'Sullivan's claim softens the 164lbs burden, and the strong tempo plays to her relentless staying profile.

runners_data.name: Fedneys Park
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's third runner, 89 days off and showing a poor recent form string (004-00); tongue-tied prominent type who has no wins from five sim-going starts and the layoff combined with poor current form makes it hard to promote him even with yard backing.

runners_data.name: Feet On The Ground
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing a hood, 66 days since last run for James Hannon (0/0 in 14 days); placed twice from nine sim-going starts and the trip seems fine at 20f — no jockey listed is a concern, though the patient style suits if a run materialises.

runners_data.name: Poppycon
runners_data.note: Paddy Cody's 4lb claim assists this 6-year-old who wears a tongue tie and hood; prominent racer with a reasonable placed record (0W3P in sim going) but the recent form string shows a fall and a zero, raising doubts about consistency over Chase fences in a rough race.

runners_data.name: Coole Vision
runners_data.note: OR 75 — the lowest-rated runner in the field and 52 days off; Norman Lee has 0/4 in 14 days and only two sim-going runs on record with no wins or places — very limited profile to justify optimism in a competitive 19-runner field.

runners_data.name: Itsalonglongroad
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is deeply problematic in a race set up for stamina; the 12-year-old prominent racer is 26 days fresh but the finishing-fade flag combined with age and OR 90 makes him a significant safety concern rather than a winning one.

races.paceDynamic: Mo Ghille Mar, Leave In Secret, and Claude are three confirmed front-runners in a 19-runner field, guaranteeing a strong early gallop on Good To Yielding ground over 2m1f — this will not be a dawdle. With eight runners seeking prominent positions, the initial quarter-mile will be congested and competitive, creating significant traffic dangers between the second-last and last fences where tired horses and jostling rivals will obstruct those coming from off the pace. The relentless early tempo will stretch the field quickly, testing stamina reserves on going that is softer than the official description suggests given consistent Good To Yielding readings all card. This race shape overwhelmingly favours genuine hold-up horses with proven stamina who can be produced late with one clean run, as any horse that burns energy fighting for position early in this traffic-heavy scenario will be vulnerable when the real race begins from three out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle burns out the leaders leaving a true stamina test for hold-up horses to motor through
scenarios.body: Mo Ghille Mar's front-running may create the suicidal pace that unravels the prominent brigade, allowing genuine hold-up horses to pick up the pieces from two out; Le Diablo's patient style and strong sim-going record (10/10 starts) suits this scenario perfectly as Kevin Healy can angle for a clean run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent racers sits just off the hot pace in a perfect stalking position and outstays rivals in the closing stages
scenarios.body: Stoneyford Lady or Lady Doyanne, both De Bromhead-trained and used to racing prominently at this trip, could benefit by sitting fourth or fifth and kicking clear before the traffic bunches at the final fence; the De Bromhead yard has excellent recent form (4/26 over 14 days) and both mares handle this going well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Mo Ghille Mar — winner last time out and sharp enough to steal a march — escapes the early war and controls the tempo from the front
scenarios.body: Mo Ghille Mar won over 18f on similar ground and has the highest sim-going strike rate among the leaders (11/12), so if Harry Sexton can slot into a comfortable lead ahead of Leave In Secret and Claude, the others may never muster the pace to reel him in; this scenario requires Leave In Secret and Claude to either capitulate early or get badly hampered in the early scramble.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage Late
scenarios.trigger: If the predicted prominent congestion two-three out causes fallers or interference that reshuffles the entire finishing order
scenarios.body: With eight prominent-seeking runners crammed together and jumping Chase fences at pace on softening ground, a mid-race incident could promote an unconsidered runner who escapes the trouble furthest from the rail; Roccabaker (OR 90, 145d off) and Poppycon (placed record in sim going) would benefit most from a scrambled, attritional finish.

watchPoints.text: Mo Ghille Mar, Leave In Secret, and Claude will all attempt to lead from the off — watch the first fence for a three-way clash that could cause a serious incident or unseat a rider.

The predicted prominent congestion between the 2nd-last and last fences involves up to eight runners fighting for space — Lady Doyanne and Stoneyford Lady must find a clean passage or their winning chances evaporate instantly.
Itsalonglongroad is flagged as a fader in a 19-runner chase field — his tendency to stop running late over fences creates a jumping hazard for hold-up horses like Le Diablo coming late on the inner.

Fedneys Park has 89 days off, a tongue tie, and poor recent form — De Bromhead's yard fitness is not in question but a horse returning after three months in a rough, fast-run race is a potential loose horse risk.

Le Diablo's trainer John Patrick Ryan holds a strong 14-day record (2/14) and Kevin Healy's 4lb claim brings the horse's burden to a competitive 149lbs — watch for a wide, late run to avoid the inner-rail traffic that will be dense between the last two fences.
